headline: Local opposition has forced the cancellation of at least $260 billion of US data center projects this year, Heatmap News reports.
score_reason: Pool 8 kept: a large, specific figure from an exclusive dataset, though it is one outlet's own survey and the industry has not responded.
importance_line: It shows community resistance, not only power or chips, now decides whether data centers get built, which affects residents who say no to nearby projects, local governments and developers, but the figures come from Heatmap's own survey and the industry did not comment.
summary: Heatmap News reports, from new data compiled by its market intelligence service Heatmap Pro, that at least $260 billion of US data center investment was canceled in 2026 after sustained local opposition, about half of it in the three months to 30 Sep. Heatmap says roughly $1 trillion more faces serious local opposition and that its own figures are likely an undercount, while the industry's lobby group, the Data Center Coalition, did not respond before publication.
notes: Read in full (subscription prompts skipped). Exclusive from Heatmap Pro's own survey of public records; no independent confirmation.
